page_title: Job, Site and Payout Tracking for Crews | Robotics Consulting
page_desc: I build tracking systems for small companies where the work happens on-site: construction and renovation, fit-out, installation, service calls. Site-based jobs, expenses, materials and crew payouts — instead of Excel and WhatsApp. Riga, Latvia.

problem_body: Companies where the work happens on-site tend to run into the same thing:
problem_body_mobile: Common problems for businesses with crews on-site:
problem_q1: How much you made on a site is only clear at the end — if it's clear at all
problem_q2: Output and crew payouts get calculated by hand, and it's an argument every month
problem_q3: Receipts and expenses come in from sites however they come in — some go missing
problem_q4: Everything lives in the owner's head, so there's no one to delegate to
problem_note: This is exactly what I fix — usually with one system, where data gets entered right where the work happens.

pricing_why_toggle: Why it's set up this way
pricing_why: This isn't the price of development — that's already paid for: you're deploying a ready system, not commissioning a new one. A crew here means a working group on site with one foreman login, not a fixed set of people: the tier is based on how many crews are active at once. From there the price grows with that number because of support volume, not the server, and every tier is fixed by contract.
pricing_why_mobile: Development is already paid for — the base is low. A crew means a working group on site, not a fixed set of people. From there, price grows with crew count because of support volume, not the server. Every tier is fixed by contract.
pricing_time_title: And, honestly, about the free month
pricing_time: It's my month that's free, not yours: it costs you 2–4 hours a week in person — checking rates, pulling data out of Excel, walking foremen through the first week. But after a month you decide by looking at your own sites in the system, not at my promise.
pricing_time_mobile: It's my month that's free, not yours: it costs you 2–4 hours a week in person. That's the real cost of entry, and it isn't in euros.

faq_sub: Real questions I get from business owners before their first step.
faq_a1: The system doesn't make money on its own — it shows you where you're losing it: rates below average, unbilled extra work, missing receipts. While you only have a handful of sites you can still see it; with 50–70 sites a year you can't. Call me — we'll run the numbers on yours.
faq_a2: Objecty as-is — €0 launch and the first month on your data, then from €150/month. The full table is in "How much this costs" above; what fits you specifically, I'll tell you in five minutes on the phone.
faq_q3: Do we need to have systems or vendors already selected?
faq_a3: No. I can start from scratch — picking the right tools, improving what you've got, or just working out where to begin. I'm not tied to any vendor, so the advice is about what fits your situation.
faq_q4: Can you work with our existing systems and tools?
faq_a4: Yes — and usually that's the whole point. Most jobs are about connecting or improving what you already run, not ripping it out and starting over. Integrations on top of existing systems are my main thing.
faq_q6: What if it turns out nothing needs to be automated?
faq_a6: Then I'll say so. If a small process change or a spreadsheet template fixes it, that's what I'll tell you. I'm not here to build things you don't actually need.
faq_q7: What kinds of businesses do you work with?
faq_a7: I work best with companies where the work is done by people on-site, not in an office: there's already more than one crew, and tracking still runs on Excel, WhatsApp and the owner's memory. That's construction and renovation, fit-out and installation, service calls, cleaning and grounds maintenance — they all have the same problem: figuring out who did what, where, and what they're owed for it. I also work with warehouses, logistics and small manufacturing.
faq_q8: Who supports the system after launch?
faq_a8: Support is included in the €150 a month from day one: server, updates, response during business hours. An outage over a weekend when the month is closing is a working day too, not a reason to wait until Monday.
faq_a9: The stack is deliberately ordinary — Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Docker — so any developer can administer it, not just me. The source code stays mine; if getting it matters to you, that goes into the contract before work starts. But the main thing is that the system lives on your server: the database with your sites, crews and payouts is yours, you have access from day one, and you can export it any time without my involvement.
